newsitem.title: USA: Carolina Brunswick N.C. nuke boosting power.
newsitem.headline: Carolina Brunswick N.C. nuke boosting power.

text.p: Carolina Power & Light Co's 754 megawatt (MW) Brunswick nuclear power unit 2 was ascending power towards full output Wednesday after a reduction for repairs to a feedwater pump, a company spokesman said.
"We should hit 100 percent output within the next 24 hours," company spokesman Mac Harris said Wednesday morning.
The Southport, N.C., unit was reduced to about 60 percent of capacity over the weekend to investigate a vibration in one of the unit's feedwater pumps.
"We took one of the feedwater pumps out of service so we had to reduce power," Harris said.
The unit was producing at about 85 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday, the spokesman said.
The company's 767 MW Brunswick unit 1, at the same Southport site, was reducing power prior to a 35-day refueling and maintenance period scheduled to begin October 5.
The Brunswick 1 unit was operating at near 90 percent of capacity early Wednesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
